title: Copying As Defense: Protecting Images from Editing By Eliciting Model Copying
title_zh: 以复制为防御：通过诱发模型复制保护图像免受编辑

paragraphs.en: Image editors built on diffusion transformers (DiTs), such as Flux Kontext, make it possible to turn a single photograph into a convincing manipulated image, including harmful and non-consensual edits. Proactive defenses aim to prevent such manipulations by adding an imperceptible perturbation before an image is shared. Existing defenses for DiT-based in-context editors take an intuitive approach: make the output attend less to the protected reference image. But this leaves the model free to follow the edit instruction using the text and its own generated tokens, often producing a new, weakly grounded image rather than preventing the edit altogether. We find that the opposite strategy is more effective. Instead of leading the model to ignore the reference, we encourage it to copy it . Through controlled attention interventions, we show that concentrating target-token attention on the reference image in only a few early blocks is sufficient to collapse the editing behavior, causing the model to reproduce its input, often as a lossy copy, rather than execute the requested transformation. Based on this insight, we introduce Copying-as-Defense (CaD), which maximizes per-token target-to-reference attention mass in early transformer blocks. Since the attention rows are normalized, increasing reference attention suppresses the attention allocated to the text and generated canvas. Restricting the objective to early blocks also lets us truncate backpropagation path, keeping optimization cheap. Across editors and benchmarks, CaD substantially suppresses instruction-following. It reduces average edit success from 81.4 % 81.4\% on unprotected images to 24.0 % 24.0\% , a 70.6 % 70.6\% relative reduction. Compared with DeContext, the strongest baseline on average at 43.0 % 43.0\% edit success, CaD further reduces edit success by 44.3 % 44.3\% . CaD is also substantially cheaper to optimize, running roughly 1.8 1.8 – 2.0 × 2.0\times faster per step than comparable optimization-based methods.

paragraphs.en: A photograph posted online can now be transformed into a convincing manipulated image with a single natural-language instruction. The same capability that enables benign editing also lowers the barrier to harmful uses, including non-consensual sexualized imagery, impersonation, misinformation, fraud, and copyright misuse ( Li et al., 2026 ; NBC News, 2026 ; Marchal et al., 2024 ) . One response has been to protect an image before it is shared by adding a small, imperceptible perturbation designed to make downstream edits fail. This idea predates modern diffusion editors, with work disrupting GAN-based facial manipulation systems ( Ruiz et al., 2020 ) , and has since expanded to diffusion-based editing ( Salman et al., 2023 ; Choi et al., 2025 ) , unauthorized personalization Marchal et al. (2024) , and artistic imitation ( Liang et al., 2023 ; Shan et al., 2023 ; Hönig et al., 2025 ) . As generative architectures evolve, however, the mechanism a defense must disrupt evolves with them.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，只需一条自然语言指令，一张发布到网上的照片就能被转换成一张令人信服的篡改图像。 同一种既能实现良性编辑的能力，也降低了有害用途的门槛，包括未经同意的性化图像、冒充、虚假信息、欺诈以及版权滥用（Li et al., 2026；NBC News, 2026；Marchal et al., 2024）。 一种应对方法是在图像分享之前对其进行保护，即添加一个微小的、不可察觉的扰动，旨在使后续编辑失败。 这一思想早于现代扩散编辑器，最初是破坏基于 GAN 的人脸操纵系统的工作（Ruiz et al., 2020），此后已扩展到基于扩散的编辑（Salman et al., 2023；Choi et al., 2025）、未经授权的个性化 Marchal et al. （2024）以及艺术模仿（Liang et al., 2023；Shan et al., 2023；Hönig et al., 2025）。 然而，随着生成式架构的演进，防御必须破坏的机制也随之演变。

paragraphs.en: That shift is especially important for the latest generation of diffusion transformers (DiTs) ( Peebles & Xie, 2023 ; Chen et al., 2024 ; Ma et al., 2024 ) . A DiT replaces the convolutional U-Net backbone with a transformer operating on latent patches ( Peebles & Xie, 2023 ) . Multimodal DiTs (MMDiT), introduced with Stable Diffusion 3, instead use separate weights for text and image tokens and let information flow in both directions between them ( Esser et al., 2024 ) . Models such as Flux Kontext and FIBO Edit mix such double-stream blocks, which keep modality-specific weights and mix tokens through attention over their concatenation, with single-stream blocks that subsequently process the concatenated sequence ( Black Forest Labs, 2025 ; Gutflaish et al., 2025 ) . Editors built on this design condition on a reference image by concatenating its tokens with the noisy output canvas along the sequence dimension. For adversarial protection, this architectural change matters twice because the representation we want to disrupt has changed, and backpropagating through a multi-billion-parameter editor is expensive.
paragraphs.zh: 这一转变对于最新一代扩散Transformer（DiT）尤为重要（Peebles & Xie, 2023；Chen et al., 2024；Ma et al., 2024）。 DiT 用在潜空间补丁上运行的 Transformer 取代了卷积 U-Net 主干（Peebles & Xie, 2023）。 随 Stable Diffusion 3 推出的多模态 DiT（MMDiT）则对文本词元和图像词元使用各自独立的权重，并允许信息在两者之间双向流动（Esser et al., 2024）。 诸如 Flux Kontext 和 FIBO Edit 等模型将这类双流块与单流块混合使用：双流块保留各模态专属的权重，并通过在二者拼接结果上做注意力来混合词元；单流块随后处理拼接后的序列（Black Forest Labs, 2025；Gutflaish et al., 2025）。 基于此设计构建的编辑器通过将参考图像的词元沿序列维度与带噪的输出画布词元拼接来对其进行条件化。 对于对抗性保护而言，这一架构变化在两个方面都很重要：因为我们要干扰的表示已经改变，并且通过一个数十亿参数规模的编辑器进行反向传播代价高昂。

paragraphs.en: Recent work therefore attacks the mechanism through which an in-context editor reads its reference. DeContext ( Shen et al., 2025 ) suppresses target-to-reference attention, aiming to decontextualize generation. The intuition is that if the output cannot attend to the protected image, then it cannot edit it. But should protection actually make the editor forget the reference?
paragraphs.zh: 因此，近期的工作开始攻击上下文编辑器读取其参考内容的机制。 DeContext（Shen et al., 2025）抑制目标对参考的注意力，旨在使生成去上下文化。 其直觉是：如果输出无法注意到受保护的图像，那么它就无法对其进行编辑。 但保护真的应该让编辑器遗忘参考内容吗？

sents.zh: 因此，近期的工作开始攻击上下文编辑器读取其参考内容的机制。

sents.en: DeContext ( Shen et al., 2025 ) suppresses target-to-reference attention, aiming to decontextualize generation.

sents.en: The intuition is that if the output cannot attend to the protected image, then it cannot edit it.
sents.zh: 其直觉是：如果输出无法注意到受保护的图像，那么它就无法对其进行编辑。

sents.en: But should protection actually make the editor forget the reference?
sents.zh: 但保护真的应该让编辑器遗忘参考内容吗？

paragraphs.en: We find that reference suppression is not only insufficient, but can be counterproductive. Each softmax attention row sums to one, so reducing attention to reference tokens reallocates probability mass to the text instruction and the evolving target canvas, which are precisely the pathways that support instruction following and generation. A successfully “decontextualized” editor can therefore still satisfy a malicious prompt by generating content that is less grounded in the protected input. Moreover, recent interpretability work on FLUX.2 shows that text tokens absorb reference content within the first few blocks and carry it to the output even when the reference is removed from the computation afterwards ( Ge et al., 2026 ) . Suppression applied after this point therefore cannot remove what has already been absorbed, so a conservative defense should avoid this residual leakage altogether rather than attenuate it downstream. This failure is particularly visible for edits the model can plausibly generate without relying on the image at all ( i.e. , ones with strong generative prior). It also fails on full-body photographs, where the person, and especially sensitive identity such as the face, occupies only a small fraction of the reference tokens.
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，抑制参考信息不仅不充分，甚至可能适得其反。 每一行 softmax 注意力的权重之和为一，因此降低对参考 token 的注意力会将概率质量重新分配给文本指令和不断演化的目标画布，而这二者恰恰是支持指令遵循与生成的通路。 因此，一个成功“去语境化”的编辑器仍然可以通过生成与受保护输入关联较弱的内容来满足恶意提示。 此外，近期针对 FLUX.2 的可解释性研究表明，文本 token 在前几个块中就会吸收参考内容，即使之后参考图像从计算中被移除，这些 token 仍会将其携带到输出中（Ge 等，2026）。 因此，在此节点之后施加的抑制无法清除已被吸收的内容，所以保守的防御策略应当彻底避免这种残余泄漏，而不是在下游对其进行衰减。 对于模型完全无需依赖图像也能合理生成的编辑（即具有强生成先验的编辑），这种失效尤为明显。 它在全身人像照片上也会失效，因为人物、尤其是面部等敏感身份信息，仅占参考 token 的很小一部分。

paragraphs.en: We therefore invert the objective. Rather than optimizing a perturbation that causes the editor to use the protected image less , we ask what happens if it is forced to use the image more . Our controlled interventions on Flux Kontext reveal that forcing target queries to place their attention on reference keys in only a few early double-stream blocks causes the model to reproduce the reference rather than execute the edit. Conversely, explicitly removing reference attention does not prevent generation. Even with a black reference image, the same qualitative distinction exists, i.e. , forcing target ⇒ \Rightarrow reference attention yields the black input itself, whereas suppressing that attention still lets the model generate a new image. An output we want is therefore not forgetting, but copying .
paragraphs.zh: 因此，我们对目标进行了反转。 与其优化一个让编辑器更少使用受保护图像的扰动，我们想知道如果强制它更多地使用该图像会发生什么。 我们对 Flux Kontext 进行的受控干预表明，仅在少数早期的双流模块中强制目标查询将注意力放在参考键上，就会使模型复现参考图像而不是执行编辑。 相反，显式移除参考注意力并不能阻止生成。 即使参考图像是黑色图像，同样的定性差异依然存在，即：强制目标 ⇒ 参考注意力会生成黑色输入本身，而抑制该注意力仍能让模型生成一张新图像。 因此，我们想要的结果不是遗忘，而是复制。

sents.en: We therefore invert the objective.
sents.zh: 因此，我们对目标进行了反转。

sents.en: Rather than optimizing a perturbation that causes the editor to use the protected image less , we ask what happens if it is forced to use the image more .

sents.en: Our controlled interventions on Flux Kontext reveal that forcing target queries to place their attention on reference keys in only a few early double-stream blocks causes the model to reproduce the reference rather than execute the edit.
sents.zh: 我们对 Flux Kontext 进行的受控干预表明，仅在少数早期的双流模块中强制目标查询将注意力放在参考键上，就会使模型复现参考图像而不是执行编辑。

sents.en: Conversely, explicitly removing reference attention does not prevent generation.

sents.en: Even with a black reference image, the same qualitative distinction exists, i.e. , forcing target ⇒ \Rightarrow reference attention yields the black input itself, whereas suppressing that attention still lets the model generate a new image.
sents.zh: 即使参考图像是黑色图像，同样的定性差异依然存在，即：强制目标 ⇒ 参考注意力会生成黑色输入本身，而抑制该注意力仍能让模型生成一张新图像。

sents.en: An output we want is therefore not forgetting, but copying .
sents.zh: 因此，我们想要的结果不是遗忘，而是复制。

paragraphs.en: This observation motivates CaD. For every target query, CaD drives target-to-reference attention mass toward one in a small set of early double-stream blocks. The objective has three useful consequences. First, attention normalization makes the reference compete directly with the text and target tokens, suppressing instruction following without needing to predict the future malicious prompt. Second, the objective is per token, preventing small identity regions from being washed out by an image-level average. Third, early-layer targeting makes the protection computationally efficient by construction. Once the last protected block is reached, we can truncate the forward pass at the last selected block and backpropagate only through this shallow set of layers, rather than differentiating through the billion-scale model. This shortened backpropagation path substantially reduces the cost of every optimization step.

paragraphs.en: Our contributions are: First , we identify two failures of attention-suppression defenses for multimodal DiT editors: mass redistribution , which leaves the text and target pathways free to render instruction-adjacent outputs similar to text-to-image generation with weak or no image conditioning, and token coverage , which makes image-averaged suppression poorly suited to full-body images. Second , through causal attention interventions, we show that the opposite direction is far more effective, i.e. , forcing early target-to-reference attention makes the editor copy its reference rather than edit it. Third , we introduce CaD, a per-token copy objective applied to early double-stream blocks. This placement is central to the method as it both induces copying and lets us truncate the model after the selected blocks, dramatically shortening the forward/backward path for each protection step. Lastly , we show that CaD substantially improves protection over existing baselines while retaining comparable imperceptibility and reducing protection time.

paragraphs.en: Different harms motivate different protections. There are many ways an unauthorized image edit can be harmful, and consequently many ways researchers have tried to protect images from such edits. When the concern is misuse of a person’s identity or face, prior work has proposed protections against facial manipulation and personalized generation ( Le et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2024 ) . When the concern is artistic style mimicry, methods such as Glaze ( Shan et al., 2023 ) , Mist ( Liang & Wu, 2023 ; Zheng et al., 2025 ) , and related approaches protect an artist’s work from being used to reproduce their style. Other methods target more general image manipulation, including inpainting and instruction-based editing ( Salman et al., 2023 ; Choi et al., 2025 ; Jeon et al., 2025 ) . In other words, “protecting an image” is not a single objective because what should be disrupted depends on what an attacker is trying to preserve, modify, or generate. At the same time, a growing body of work has questioned how much protection these methods provide outside the particular threat models for which they were designed ( Li et al., 2026 ; Hönig et al., 2025 ; Radiya-Dixit et al., 2021 ) . Protections that are effective against one manipulation may offer little protection against another, making broad claims of image protection difficult.

paragraphs.en: Protection is a moving target. Two broader challenges make proactive protection particularly difficult. First, generative models continue to evolve. A protection designed around one model family may no longer target the representations or mechanisms used by its successors, requiring defenses to evolve alongside the models they are intended to protect. Second, adversarial perturbations are inherently vulnerable to transformations of the protected image. Even ordinary processing, such as JPEG compression, resizing, or added noise, can weaken a perturbation, while an adversary can intentionally apply more sophisticated purification procedures designed to remove it ( Hönig et al., 2025 ) . These limitations do not eliminate the value of proactive protection, but they make it important to be precise about both the model and the manipulation against which a defense is evaluated.

paragraphs.en: Protecting images from modern DiT editors. Recent image editors increasingly replace the UNet backbone used by earlier latent diffusion models with diffusion transformers (DiTs) and related multimodal transformer architectures ( Peebles & Xie, 2023 ; Esser et al., 2024 ) . Models such as FLUX.1 Kontext ( Black Forest Labs, 2025 ) , Step1X-Edit ( Liu et al., 2025 ) , and FIBO Edit ( Gutflaish et al., 2025 ) perform instruction-based editing by jointly processing the reference image, the text instruction, and the image being generated. To the best of our knowledge, DeContext ( Shen et al., 2025 ) is the only existing proactive protection method designed specifically around this new class of in-context DiT editors. This does not mean that earlier protection methods cannot be applied to newer editors. Rather, they were not designed specifically for their architecture.

paragraphs.en: We therefore evaluate representative approaches from several existing families after adapting them to FLUX.1 Kontext and FIBO Edit. PhotoGuard ( Salman et al., 2023 ) perturbs the image so that its latent under the model’s VAE matches that of a mid-gray image. DeContext ( Shen et al., 2025 ) minimizes the attention that the generated image’s tokens place on the reference image’s tokens; for FIBO Edit, which takes structured JSON prompts, a VLM is called once per edit instruction on the clean image to produce them. Diff-PGD proposed as a baseline ( Shen et al., 2025 ) maximizes the flow-matching error the model makes when reconstructing a clean edit from the perturbed reference image, where the clean edit for each instruction is generated once with the editor itself and cached; for FIBO Edit, each edit is generated from a VLM-produced JSON prompt, so this also requires one VLM call per instruction. Our method also operates on attention, but starts from a different observation about how reference information should be manipulated. Rather than suppressing the reference image, we ask whether the model can be made to rely on it more . This distinction motivates the analysis in Sections 3 – 5 .
paragraphs.zh: 因此，我们在将现有几类代表性方法适配到 FLUX.1 Kontext 和 FIBO Edit 之后，对它们进行评估。 PhotoGuard（Salman et al., 2023）对图像进行扰动，使其在模型 VAE 下的潜变量与一张中灰色图像的潜变量相匹配。 DeContext（Shen et al., 2025）最小化生成图像的 token 对参考图像 token 的注意力；对于采用结构化 JSON 提示词的 FIBO Edit，每条编辑指令会对干净图像调用一次 VLM 来生成这些提示词。 Diff-PGD 作为基线被提出（Shen et al., 2025），它最大化模型在从被扰动的参考图像重建干净编辑时的流匹配误差，其中每条指令的干净编辑由编辑器本身生成一次并缓存；对于 FIBO Edit，每次编辑都从 VLM 生成的 JSON 提示词产生，因此这同样需要对每条指令调用一次 VLM。 我们的方法同样作用于注意力，但出发点是关于应如何操纵参考信息的一个不同观察。 我们不是抑制参考图像，而是探究能否让模型更加依赖它。 这一区别推动了第 3–5 节的分析。

sents.zh: 如图 1 所示，抑制可能会破坏紧密裁剪人脸的身份保持，但仍能成功编辑受保护的全身主体。

paragraphs.en: A key reason is token coverage . In Flux Kontext, the VAE downsamples spatially by 8 × 8\times and its latents are packed into 2 × 2 2\times 2 patches, so a 512 × 512 512\times 512 image produces a 32 × 32 32\times 32 grid of 1024 image tokens, each corresponding to a 16 × 16 16\times 16 pixel region. In Fig. 1 (a), 944 of 1024 tokens (92%) belong primarily to the subject, so an image-averaged suppression objective necessarily acts on subject information. In Fig. 1 (b), only 322 tokens (31%) belong primarily to the person and just 7 × 7 = 49 7\times 7=49 tokens (4.8%) cover the face. This is representative of BodyBench more broadly as the face-and-body mask occupies only 28.45 % ± 6.06 % 28.45\%\pm 6.06\% of the image area on average. Thus, an objective averaged over all target–reference interactions can be driven down largely through background tokens while leaving comparatively few identity related interactions intact.
paragraphs.zh: 一个关键原因是词元覆盖率。 在 Flux Kontext 中，VAE 在空间上按 8 × 8\times 下采样，其潜变量被打包为 2 × 2 2\times 2 的图像块，因此一张 512 × 512 512\times 512 的图像会产生一个 32 × 32 32\times 32 的网格，共 1024 个图像词元，每个词元对应一个 16 × 16 16\times 16 像素的区域。 在图 1 (a) 中，1024 个词元中有 944 个（92%）主要属于主体，因此对图像取平均的抑制目标必然会作用于主体信息。 在图 1 (b) 中，只有 322 个词元（31%）主要属于该人物，而仅有 7 × 7 = 49 7\times 7=49 个词元（4.8%）覆盖面部。 这在整个 BodyBench 中具有代表性，因为人脸与身体的掩码平均仅占图像面积的 28.45 % ± 6.06 % 28.45\%\pm 6.06\%。 因此，一个对所有目标—参考交互取平均的目标，可能主要通过与背景词元相关的部分被压低，而让相对较少的与身份相关的交互保持不变。

paragraphs.en: Two additional properties make reference suppression an incomplete objective. First, attention mass is redistributed : by Eq. 3 , reducing reference attention necessarily reallocates mass to text and target keys. The editor can therefore remain strongly driven by the instruction and its evolving target representation even when grounding in the reference is weakened. Second, reference information can move between token groups . Recent analysis of FLUX.2 shows that text tokens absorb visual information from the reference within early blocks and can subsequently carry that information toward the output ( Ge et al., 2026 ) . Removing a direct target-to-reference interaction therefore does not imply that reference information has been removed from the computation.
paragraphs.zh: 另外两个性质使得抑制参考成为一个不完整的目标。 第一，注意力质量会被重新分配：根据公式 3，减少参考注意力必然会将质量重新分配给文本键和目标键。 因此，即使对参考的依赖被削弱，编辑器仍然可以强烈地受指令及其不断演进的目标表示驱动。 第二，参考信息可以在不同词元组之间流动。 对 FLUX.2 的近期分析表明，文本词元会在早期块中吸收来自参考的视觉信息，并随后将该信息传递到输出（Ge et al., 2026）。 因此，移除目标与参考之间的直接交互并不意味着参考信息已从计算中被移除。

paragraphs.en: Figure 2 makes the contrast between the two intervention directions visually clear. Removing target-to-reference attention does not stop the model from producing plausible edits that follow the instruction. Forcing target-to-reference attention, however, progressively changes the output from an edit into a reproduction of the reference as the intervention is applied across more early blocks. The principle holds even when the input image is a purely black image (the black-reference control in Fig. 2(a) ): suppressing reference attention still allows the model to generate instruction-consistent content, whereas forcing reference attention causes the output to collapse toward the black reference.
paragraphs.zh: 图 2 直观地展示了这两种干预方向之间的对比。 移除目标到参考的注意力并不会阻止模型生成符合指令的合理编辑。 然而，强制目标到参考的注意力会随着干预被应用到更多早期模块而逐步将输出从编辑变为对参考图像的复现。 即使输入图像是纯黑图像（图 2(a) 中的黑参考对照），该原理依然成立：抑制参考注意力仍能让模型生成与指令一致的内容，而强制参考注意力则会使输出坍缩向黑参考。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate protection effectiveness using Edit Success Rate (ESR), PickScore, CLIP directional similarity (CLIP dir ), and ArcFace similarity. ESR is the fraction of edited outputs judged successful by Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct ( Bai et al., 2025 ) , which jointly considers the original image, edited image, edit instruction, and intended edited description. An edit is successful only if it realizes the requested transformation while preserving unrelated content and identity and avoiding major visual artifacts. PickScore ( Kirstain et al., 2023 ) measures alignment between the edited image and a target caption describing the requested edit. CLIP dir ( Gal et al., 2022 ) measures whether the change from the original to the edited image follows the corresponding semantic change in text embedding space. ArcFace ( Deng et al., 2019 ) measures identity similarity between the faces in the original and edited images. Lower values indicate stronger protection for all four metrics. We measure protection perceptibility between the original image and protected image using LPIPS ( Zhang et al., 2018 ) and PSNR, where lower LPIPS and higher PSNR indicate a less perceptible perturbation. We additionally report computational efficiency using the median time per optimization step, T S T_{S} in seconds, and the resulting optimization time per protection, T P T_{P} in minutes.

paragraphs.en: Table 1 and Fig. 3 summarize our main results at ϵ = 12 / 255 \epsilon=12/255 . Across both editors, CaD strongly disrupts the requested edit without requiring larger perturbations than the other optimization-based defenses. The clearest gains appear on Flux Kontext. On BodyBench, CaD reduces edit success to 5.1 % 5.1\% , compared with 24.9 % 24.9\% for DeContext and 44.2 % 44.2\% for Diff-PGD. CLIP dir falls to 0.0359 0.0359 , far below the next-best protected result of 0.2574 0.2574 . We see the same pattern on InpaintGuardBench, where CaD reaches 16.0 % 16.0\% edit success and a CLIP dir score of 0.0513 0.0513 . The qualitative examples in Fig. 3 match this behavior: while the baselines often still carry out the requested transformation, our protected outputs tend to remain close to the original input. We note the decontextualization behavior of DeContext in the third row of Fig. 3 where the identity of the original subject is not present in the edit, yet the unconditional generation (as if using a black reference) is still generated. Based on the intuition discussed in section 4 , we would still see to avoid this behavior.

The same advantage holds on FIBO, where CaD takes 0.754 0.754 s per step and 12.57 12.57 min per protection. Figure 5 further shows that the full optimization budget is often unnecessary: by 300 steps, CaD already outperforms the final 800-step baselines across all four protection metrics, corresponding to only about 3.2 3.2 minutes of optimization on Flux Kontext.

paragraphs.en: Block selection. Our intervention study suggests that the copying behavior is established early in the network. paragraphs.en: Objective direction. We finally isolate the direction of the attention objective. paragraphs.en: Modern in-context image editors make heavy use of the reference image, so existing defenses have naturally tried to protect that image by making the model attend to it less. We find that this is often the wrong direction. Suppressing reference attention can leave the model free to follow the instruction, particularly when the protected subject occupies only a small fraction of the image. Controlled interventions reveal a different behavior when reference attention is increased. Once target tokens are made to rely strongly on the reference in the early transformer blocks, the model begins to reproduce the input instead of editing it. We turn this observation into CaD, a protection objective that increases target-to-reference attention for each target token in a small set of early blocks. Across FLUX Kontext and FIBO Edit, CaD provides stronger protection than existing baselines while maintaining comparable perturbation quality, and its early-layer objective makes optimization considerably cheaper. Our results suggest that protecting images from modern editors need not mean hiding the reference from the model. Making the model rely on it more can itself be a defense.

paragraphs.en: Limitations. Our evaluation is limited to two DiT-based editors. Like other optimization-based proactive defenses, CaD also assumes white-box access to the protected editor during perturbation construction and requires per-image optimization, despite being substantially cheaper than deeper attention- or denoiser-based objectives. Finally, adversarial image protections can be weakened by common transformations such as compression, resizing, or noise, and by deliberate purification procedures; we do not evaluate robustness against such adaptive preprocessing or attacks here.

paragraphs.en: We compare four protection methods (PhotoGuard, DeContext, Diff-PGD, and ours) on two image-editing models, FLUX.1 Kontext-dev and FIBO Edit. All methods perturb the context/reference (to-be-protected) image x x with the same projected gradient descent (PGD) procedure and differ only in the loss they optimize.
